framework.name: 1. An economy that innovates, generates employment and promotes sustainable development

children.name: 1.1. Promotes a transition towards sustainable production systems and consumption patterns, based on innovation, scientific knowledge and making use of technology, strengthening resilience and equity.

1.1.1. Sustainable production and consumption models developped and validated in strategic sectors of the economy, that include and test new technologies/practices following the principles of circular economy, strengthen the development of the bioeconomy and favour resilience and inclusion.

1.1.2. Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures designed and validated to increase climate goals, promote low-carbon development and energy transition, strengthen resilience and social inclusion, adopting a transversal perspective towards gender integration.
1.1.3. New technologies promoted and validated that enable the country to make progress towards the second energy transition through decarbonization of the transport and industrial sectors.
1.1.4. Designed and validated environmental management and restoration measures that strengthen ecosystem services and improve the resilience of territories and communities.

1.2. Consolidate economic recuperation based on the generation of quality and decent jobs, and the promotion of the entrepreneurial capacity of the private sector, in particular of small and medium businesses, increasing the participation of women in the economy.

1.2.1. Strengthened institutions of the Ministry of Labour and Social Security in the design and management of active employment policies for the sectors most affected by the crisis and in productive transformation with social inclusion.
1.2.2. Strengthened capacities of organisations in charge of the design and implementation of employment and professional training policies to identify skill gaps and anticipate training demands.
children.description: 1.2.2. "Capacidades de los organismos a cargo del diseño y ejecución de políticas de empleo, formación profesional y capacitación fortalecidas para identificar brechas de competencias y anticipar demandas de formación."

children.name: 1.2.3. Strengthened capacities of the Ministry of Labour and Social Security and of the INEFOP in the design and management of innovative training strategies and modalities, particularly those based on partnerships between training institutes and businesses, to develop capacities and competencies of workers and improve the productivity of companies.

1.2.4. Strengthened capacities of businesses in the implementation of sustainable corporate management, with a gender perspective, promoting an inclusive corporate ecosystem and increasing the participation of women in the economy.
1.3. Create an ecosystem for the financing of development that adopts a gender perspective and fosters public-private partnerships to achieve SDGs in Uruguay.

1.3.2. Installed and functioning financial instrument to promote the second energy transition from renewable energies, incorporating a gender perspective, in coordination with comercial and multilateral banks.

1.3.1.Strengthened capacities of the national ecosystem for the financing of development, with a gender perspective, to promote partnerships between public and private actors and to harmonize the investment flows and initiatives with the introduction of innovative, sustainable and inclusive solutions.

framework.name: 2. An efficient government, present in the territories and that is accountable to its citizens

children.name: 2.1. Modernize public sector management, foster decentralization and the participation of citizens by improving accountability processes and government transparency.

2.1.1. Implemented modernization process in the public sector and consolidated institutional transformations in the three branches of the state, with an emphasis on capacity development and re-engineering of institutional structures, the introduction of new organisational structures in ministries and of a reform of the civil service to improve planification and the management of human resources with a focus on hiring, continuous training and development of high level professionals, to progress towards a eficient public management with a quality public spending, geared towards the monitoring and accomplishment of strategic results.

2.1.2. Decentralization strategy deepened through the promotion of effective cooperation and coordination between different levels of government, local actors, members of parliament and development of capacities and competencies of a new generation and professionalized local management (including in monitoring and evaluation) to steer transformations towards enhanced territorial equity, as a result of a public policy that promotes the digitalization of government services.

2.1.3. Accountability mechanisms in place in different levels of government, able to deepen and expand transparency in public management, and to improve confidence of citizens in actors and satisfaction in public services, with a focus on the development, implementation and monitoring of open government plans, access to public information, bringing parliament closer to citizens, inclusive governance, institutionalized public consultation spaces and substantial citizenship participation of the organized civil society, considering specific groups such as teenagers and youngsters. Strengthened monitoring and accountability mechanisms in independant institutions and civil society, including the media and human rights defenders.
2.2. Strengthen the capacity of the government to prevent and address violence, protect security and promotes citizen coexistence.

2.2.1.Social cohesion strategy designed and public policies implemented in the framework of a new social contract, with an emphasis on the development of the capacity of public actors and the consolidation of new partnerships (including civil society and the private sector) to prevent different forms of violence that affect the most vulnerable groups, adressing conflicts and urban violence in a way that contributes to the creation of public spaces of integration (between and within generations, ethnies, migrants) which are safe, free of violence and inclusive (eradicating all forms of violence), accessible and usable by all (particularly those that are the most excluded, such as disabled persons) and that also contribute to the generation of infrastructures and programs that promote education, culture, communication, sports and recreation as relevant dimensions.

2.2.2. Public policies reviewed to reflect evidence-based knowledge (identifying lessons learned from international experience) and reflecting normative frameworks on human rights, renovated institutional structures and developped government capacities to effectively address the challenges of existing imprisonment schemes, with a special emphasis on schemes of deprivation of freedom (teenagers, adults), of mental health and progressing towards the necessary transformations to address the needs of persons that transit through total institutions (including the component of protection of children and teenagers).

2.2.3. Integral strategies (based on the concept of human security) designed, knowledge generated and made available from international experience and implementation of public policies within the framework of an agenda that considers new forms of crime and organized crime, possession of weapons by civilians, drug traficking, among others, and its impacts on vulnerable population groups, particularly young men and women, considering the territorial perspective (country borders as critical territories) and promoting the connection of the different dimensions involved in public policies geared towards development.

2.3. Strengthen institutional capacities to manage and analyze information (with an emphasis on disaggregations by sex and other key socio-demographic variables) useful for decision-making, the design and evaluation of policies and the provision of services.

2.3.1. Strengthened capacities of the National Statistical System for the generation and dissemination of socio-economic and demographic information at the highest possible territorial disaggregation, through the support to the improvements to the different components of information systems (population census, household surveys, use and interoperability of administrative registries).

2.3.2. Inter-institutional model designed and implemented with the support of the Un System for the analysis and use of socio-economic and demographic information for evidence-based decision-making, in support to the design, monitoring and evaluation of public policies of development in the medium and long-term of the country's path towards the accomplishment of the 2030 Agenda.

framework.name: 3. Public policies that ensure education, social protection and quality health for all persons

children.name: 3.1. The education system in Uruguay initiates an integral transformation of basic education (from primary to secondary school) to ensure access, avoid drop-outs, improve learning and reduce inequalities in results between socio-economic groups (including afro-descendants and persons with discapacities), and expand tertiary education, increasing the participation of women in science, technology and engineering.

3.1.1. Strengthened capacities of the education system to ensure that all children and teenagers have access to an inclusive, innovative and quality education, culminating in a mandatory education based on integral training, including transversal and self-care capacities.

3.1.2. Alternative modalities developped, piloted and validated for the termination of mandatory education and for continuing education that take into account the competencies necessary in the labour market and integrate businesses in the training system.

3.1.3. Adopted and validated strategies and initiatives to increment enrollments in tertiary and universitary education, especially in Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics programs, promoting in particular the participation of women in the latter, and the inclusion of vulnerable population groups, including actions that facilitate the recognition and certification of studies conducted abroad.

3.2. The Integrated National Health System improves primary health care and public-private complementarity, in the framework of the post-Covid 19 recuperation, as well as prevention programs on chronic non transmissible diseases and the quality and universality of sexual and reproductive health services, with a focus on women and youngsters from the most vulnerable groups.

3.2.1. A Strategy has been defined to make progress towards the National Sanitary Goals for the five-year period, with an emphasis on prioritized non-transmissible diseases, food security, child development in early childhood and integral health of teenagers.
children.description: 3.2.1. "Se ha definido la estrategia para avanzar en Objetivos Sanitarios Nacionales para el quinquenio, con énfasis en líneas de acción para problemas priorizados en el campo de las enfermedades no transmisibles, la seguridad alimentaria, el desarrollo infantil en la primera infancia y la salud integral de los adolescentes."

children.name: 3.2.2. Mechanisms of response to emergencies and disasters have been developped, incorporating the lessons learned from COVID-19, centered in the sistematization of knowledge and scientific evidence in responses, vigilance in public health, timely response of the health system, of social support and of essential services, mechanisms of care and strengthening of communitary organizations.
children.description: 3.2.2. "Se han desarrollado mecanismos de respuesta a emergencias y desastres que incorporan las lecciones aprendidas de COVID-19, centrados en la sistematización del conocimiento y la evidencia científica en las respuestas, vigilancia en salud pública, respuesta oportuna del sistema de salud, soporte social y de los servicios esenciales, dispositivos de cuidados y fortalecimiento de la organización comunitaria."

children.name: 3.2.3. Problem-solving capacities of health services have been strengthened from primary attention, through improvements in coordination and complementarity between public and private providers of the National Integrated Health System, the reduction in its fragmentation and segmentation, and the maximization of the quality of services, as well as through effectiveness and efficiency of the entire system

3.2.4. In collaboration with the healthcare system, development, testing and validation of programs aiming at ensuring universal access to integral services of Sexual and Reproductive Health, as well as at ensuring access to prevention and attention for HIV, gender and generation-based violence, with a homogeneous coverage and quality across the national territory.
3.3. Create new public policy frameworks and governance models that promote social protection and cohesion as well as multidimensional well-being.

3.3.1. Developped, tested and validated social protection models geared towards equity, universality and financial and social sustainability, incorporating lessons learned from the COVID-19 pandemic, with an emphasis on renovating the gender and generational contract, strengthening of the healthcare pillars, reforming the social security system and decent and inclusive work.
children.description: 3.3.1. "Se han desarrollado, probado y validado modelos de protección social orientados por la equidad, universalidad y sostenibilidad financiera y social, incorporando las lecciones aprendidas en el proceso de la pandemia COVID 19, con énfasis en la renovación del contrato de género y generaciones, el fortalecimiento del pilar de cuidados, la reforma del sistema seguridad social y el trabajo decente e inclusivo."

children.name: 3.3.2. National and subnational capacities have been deepened and expanded to develop social protection actions with an emphasis on transforming gender relations and generational perspective, strengthening resilience of the population in general and in particular vulnerable persons (families with dependent children, LGTBIQ+, persons deprived of freedom, afrodescendants, disabled persons, migrants and refugees).
children.description: 3.3.2. "Se ha profundizado y expandido las capacidades a nivel nacional y subnacional para desarrollar acciones de protección social, con énfasis en la transformación de las relaciones de género y perspectiva generacional, fortaleciendo resiliencia de la población en general y en particular de las personas en situación de vulnerabilidad (familias con niños y niñas a cargo, LGTBIQ+, personas privadas de libertad, afrodescendientes, personas con discapacidad, migrantes y refugiadas)"

children.name: 3.3.3. Consolidated capacities to respond to the challenges posed by socio-territorial segregation in urban areas, as well as in the urban-rural interface, with an emphasis on the social and housing conditions of the most vulnerable populations (residents in illegal settlements, precarious consolidated cities and rural areas), strengthening communitary networks, mobility opportunities, substantial participation of citizens and urban development geared towards social integration (inclusive and quality public spaces and basic services).
children.description: 3.3.3. "Se han consolidado capacidades para responder a los desafíos de la segregación socio territorial a nivel urbano, así como en la interfase urbano-rural con énfasis en las condiciones socio habitacionales de la población más vulnerable (residentes en asentamientos irregulares, ciudad consolidada precaria y áreas rurales), fortalecimiento de redes comunitarias, oportunidades de movilidad, participación ciudadana sustantiva y desarrollo urbano orientado a la integración social (espacios públicos y servicios básicos inclusivos y de calidad) "

framework.name: 4. A society that promotes development, human rights and that leaves no one behind

children.name: 4.1. National and subnational public institutions, the private sector, social actors and comunities in Uruguay make progress in eliminating the persistent gender gaps and in facilitating a sociocultural change necessary to enhance the participation of women in decision-making and to eradicate gender-based violence.

4.1.1. Strengthened capacities of public institutions (national and subnational), with an emphasis on the institute in charge of gender policies and on civil society organizations that advocate for the rights of women, to improve the design of policies and programs based on evidence and aiming at eliminating gender gaps.

4.1.2. Advocacy strategy developped, partnerships strengthened and actions implemented to broaden the participation of women in decision-making positions in national and local government, political parties and parliament, as well as development of initiatives with the private sector, cooperatives and unions to broaden the participation of women in decision-making positions in these organizations.

4.1.3. Strengthened prevention, care and remediation mechanisms, stressing the elimination of violent and discriminatory cultural patterns that sustain gender stereotypes and affect the most vulnerable groups.

4.2. Public institutions, the private sector, the civil society and families in Uruguay strengthen their capacities to protect the rights and well-being of boys, girls, teenagers and youngsters, in particular those in greatest state of vulnerability.

4.2.1. Capacities of national and sub-national actors strengthened on the design, implementation and monitoring of normative frameworks, public policies and social programs that ensure, promote and protect the rights of children, teenagers and youngsters with a focus on the following areas: early childhood, prevention of separation from family, sexual and reproductive health, education and training for employment.

4.2.2.  Institutional mechanisms strengthened to prevent, detect and support children and teenagers at risk of violence, to facilitate their access to specialized justice and to adequately monitor the situation, supporting at the same time interventions that contribute to develop the capacities of families (ensuring the right of children to live in a family, including adoptive ones), caregivers and personal from institutions as well as to develop spaces for intersectoral coordination.

4.3. The Uruguayan government creates normative frameworks and strengthens institutions and policies to protect the rights of the most relegated populations groups (afrodescendents, persons with disabilities, from LGTBI groups, homeless persons, migrants and refugees) and combats the stigmatization and discrimination that they suffer.

4.3.1. Capacities of the three branches of government (executive, legislative, judicial) strengthened on the design, implementation and evaluation of normative frameworks and public policies geared towards the promotion of the exercise of human rights and their full social inclusion (with a focus on the most vulnerable population groups) through technical assistance of the agencies of the SNU.

4.3.2. Transformation of social norms that sustain preconceptions and forms of discrimination based on ethno-racial descent, gender identity, disability, nationality, migratory status or other characteristics of persons throught the support to actions of sensitization and awareness-raising conducted by the agencies of the SUN.

4.3.3. Strengthened capacities on the monitoring of human rights for the most vulnerable population groups or for those that may suffer to a greater extent from the socio-economic impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic.
